correctness.rationale: For cubic Heawood H with 14 vertices and 21 edges, removing k vertices spanning e(S) edges leaves 14−k vertices and 21−3k+e(S) edges. If complement forest has c components, c=2k−7−e(S). For k<=3 a forest is impossible (c<=−1); at k=4 necessary c=1 and e(S)=0: independent four-vertex deletion leaving a ten-vertex tree. By Fano incidence: four deleted point vertices leave an acyclic graph iff retained three points collinear, giving 7 possibilities, and dual gives 7; for three deleted points and one line, independence forces deleted points outside selected line, giving 7*4=28, dual 28. In two+two split, the only deleted lines avoid both deleted points and the retained point at their join creates an isolated two-vertex component, so no optimum. All 70 complements have the indicated tree degree profiles (type A six leaves/four degree-three, type B three leaves/six degree-two/one degree-three), which distinguish orbits. The 168 collineations GL(3,2) plus polarity act transitively on lines and anti-flags, yielding full group 336 and orbit sizes 14,56. Independent brute force over 2^14=16384 Fano incidence graph subsets found exactly 70 minimum sets and split counts by removed-point number 4:7,3:28,1:28,0:7. This finite graph claim is exhaustively decidable; separate combinatorial proof also supplied.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge new exact enumeration and two-orbit classification of all minimum feedback vertex sets in the natural Heawood incidence graph. Earlier cubic counting formula and decycling lower bound are acknowledged; inaccessible highly related 2022 body is an explicit risk rather than automatic rejection.
residual_risks: Complete 2022 Nedela–Skoviera text unavailable; it could contain a Heawood-specific enumeration in a lemma or appendix.
Other unindexed Heawood induced-tree tables or equivalently phrased decycling-orbit enumerations could precede this result.
Exact result is for one 14-vertex graph and does not classify all cubic graphs or all projective-plane incidence graphs.

value.rationale: Heawood graph is a canonical incidence and highly symmetric cubic graph; exact structure of all maximum induced trees and their full automorphism orbits is a natural graph invariant with geometric interpretation. The full 70-set classification and complementary tree shapes go beyond well-known scalar decycling lower bounds; finite scope does not make it arbitrary.
